$\mathcal{N}$ denotes the nilpotent singular support condition~\cite{AG}.

By the spectral construction, 
the (semi)stable Higgs bundles correspond to compactly supported 
pure one-dimensional coherent sheaves on $S$
which are Gieseker (semi)stable~\cite{Hu} 
with respect 
to $\pi^* h$ where $h$ is an ample divisor on $C$. 
We will often use the following characterizations: 
a pure one-dimensional sheaf $E$ on $S$ corresponds to (semi)stable 
Higgs bundle if and only if for any surjection $E\twoheadrightarrow E'$
for a pure one-dimensional sheaf $E'$, we have
\begin{align}\label{ineq:surj}
    \frac{\deg \pi_{*}E}{\operatorname{rank}\pi_{*}E}<(\leqslant) 
     \frac{\deg \pi_{*}E'}{\operatorname{rank}\pi_{*}E'}. 
\end{align}

Below we often say that $E\in \operatorname{Coh}^{\heartsuit}(\mathcal{C}_b)$ is (semi)stable if it corresponds to (semi)stable Higgs bundles; equivalently if it satisfies the above inequality (\ref{ineq:surj}) for any surjection $E\twoheadrightarrow E'$ as above.

(2) For each decomposition r=r_1+cdots+r_k, we have the addition map B_GL_r_1 times cdots times B_GL_r_k to B_GL_r given by adding spectral curves as effective divisors. Then B_GL_r^A contains the image of the generic point of the above map. Indeed, for a general choice of spectral curves C_1, ldots, C_k, where C_i corresponds to b_i in B_GL_r_i, the curves C_i are smooth, and C_i and C_j intersect transversely at points which are not ramification points of the projections C_i to C and C_j to C. \emph{(\cite[Lemma~6.1]{TodaGL2})}\label{lem:perfect}
In the setting of Definition~\ref{def:Lcat}, suppose that
$\mathcal{E} \in \operatorname{Coh}(\mathfrak{M})$ is perfect. Then for a map
$\nu \colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathfrak{M}$ with image $x\in \mathfrak{M}(k)$, 
$\mathrm{wt}(\nu^*\mathcal{E})$ is contained in a bounded interval $I \subset \mathbb{R}$ 
if and only if 
$\mathrm{wt}(\iota_{*}\nu^{\mathrm{reg}*}\mathcal{E})$ is contained in 
$I+[c_1(\mathfrak{g}_x^{<0}), c_1(\mathfrak{g}_x^{>0})]$. 

In particular, $\iota_{*}\nu^{\mathrm{reg}*}\mathcal{E}$ satisfies condition~(\ref{wt:cond2}) if and only if 
$\nu^* \mathcal{E}$ satisfies the following condition:
\begin{align}\label{wt:cond2}
    \mathrm{wt}(\nu^* \mathcal{E}) \subset \left[\frac{1}{2} c_1 (\nu^{\ast}\mathbb{L}_{\mathfrak{M}}^{<0}), 
    \frac{1}{2} c_1 (\nu^{\ast}\mathbb{L}_{\mathfrak{M}}^{>0})
    \right]+c_1(\nu^{\ast}\delta).
\end{align}

\label{rmk:HN!}
More generally, 
there is a total order $\preceq$ on the set of Harder--Narasimhan types
$\mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_k)$, and a Harder--Narasimhan stratification
\[
  \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)=\sqcup_{\mu} \mathcal{S}_{\mu},
\]
where $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$ is the Harder--Narasimhan stratum of type $\mu$.
By setting
\[
  \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi):=\sqcup_{\mu'\preceq \mu}\mathcal{S}_{\mu'},
   \quad
 \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)_{\prec \mu}:=\sqcup_{\mu'\prec \mu}\mathcal{S}_{\mu'},
\]
we have a open/closed stratification
\[
    \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)_{\preceq \mu}=\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)_{\prec \mu} \sqcup \mathcal{S}_{\mu},
\]
and $\mathcal{S}_{\mu}$ is a $\Theta$-stratum of $\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)_{\preceq \mu}$.

For the open immersion
\begin{align}\label{open:ju}
   j_{\mu}\colon\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)_{\prec \mu}\hookrightarrow
  \mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)_{\preceq \mu},
\end{align}
there is a fully faithful left adjoint to $j_{\mu}^{\ast}$,
by~\cite[Theorems~7.18 and~7.19]{PTlim},
\[
     (j_{\mu})_{!}\colon
     \operatorname{L}_{\mathcal{N}}(\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)_{\prec \mu})_{w}
     \hookrightarrow
     \operatorname{L}_{\mathcal{N}}(\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}(\chi)_{\preceq \mu})_{w},
\]
whose image is described by the weight condition~\eqref{wt:cond2}, with the
left inequality strict, for any map $\nu$ of Harder--Narasimhan type $\mu$
as in~\eqref{map:nupt}.

\emph{(\cite[Lemma~2.2]{Ardual}, \cite[Lemma~2.22]{TodaGL2})}\label{lem:MCM-extension}
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a classical Artin stack of pure dimension, and let
$
M\in \operatorname{Coh}^{\heartsuit}(\mathcal{X})
$
be a maximal Cohen--Macaulay sheaf on $\mathcal{X}$. Let
$\mathcal{Z}\subset \mathcal{X}$ be a closed substack of codimension at
least two, and let
$
j\colon \mathcal{X}\setminus \mathcal{Z}\hookrightarrow \mathcal{X}
$
be the open immersion. Then the natural morphism
$
M \to j^{\heartsuit}_{*}(M|_{\mathcal{X}\setminus \mathcal{Z}})
$
is an isomorphism, where
$
j^{\heartsuit}_{*}:=\mathcal{H}^0(j_*).
$

The first statement follows since the cotangent complexes of 
$\mathcal{H}_b$, $\mathcal{H}$ differ from those of $\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}$ by the cotangent complexes of 
$k[-1]$ and $\mathcal{B}$, which have trivial $\mathbb{G}_m$-weights. 

As for the second statement, note that we have 
\begin{align*}
    \nu^* \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}} \simeq
     \nu^* \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}}=
    \operatorname{Hom}_S(M, M)[1].
\end{align*}
Therefore we have 
\begin{align*}
     \nu^* \mathbb{L}_{\mathrm{Higgs}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}}^{>0}=
     \bigoplus_{i<j}\operatorname{Hom}_S(M_j, M_i)[1]
\end{align*}
where $\operatorname{Hom}_S(M_j, M_i)[1]$ has $\mathbb{G}_m$-weight $\nu_i-\nu_j$. 
    Therefore the formula (\ref{compute:wg}) for positive part follows from 
    the following (which is computed using the Riemann-Roch formula)
    \begin{align*}
        -\chi_S(M_j, M_i)=C_i \cdot C_j=r_i r_j(2g-2).
    \end{align*}
    The computation of the negative part is the same.

\label{prop:natural}
Let $\mathcal{C}_b \subset S$ be a spectral curve corresponding to
$b \in \mathrm{B}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}^{\mathrm{cl}}$, which is not necessarily reduced. For a line
bundle $\mathcal{L}$ on $\mathcal{C}_b$ with $w'=\deg_{\mathcal{C}_b}(\mathcal{L})$, let
$\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{L}}$ be the corresponding line bundle on $\mathcal{H}_b$. Then
$\mathcal{L}$ corresponds to a semistable Higgs bundle if and only if, for
any map $\nu \colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathcal{H}_b$, we have
\begin{align}\label{nuPL}
\mathrm{wt}(\nu^* \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{L}})
\subset
\left[
 \frac{1}{2}c_1(\nu^*\mathbb{L}^{<0}_{\mathcal{H}_b}),
 \frac{1}{2}c_1(\nu^* \mathbb{L}_{\mathcal{H}_b}^{>0})
\right]
+c_1(\nu^* \delta_{w'}).
\end{align}

nodes.statement: Let nu colon BG_m to H_b be a map as in Lemma~, and set r_i=rank(pi_*O_C_i), l_i=deg_C_i(L|_C_i). For a subset Isubset \1,ldots,k\, we write C_I:=sum_iin I C_i as an effective divisor on S, and set r_I:=sum_iin Ir_i and l_I:=sum_iin Il_i. Note that wt(nu^* P_L) consists of the single element c_1(nu^* P_L)in Z, as P_L is a line bundle. Since \[ c_1(nu^* delta_w') = fracw'rsum_i=1^k r_i nu_i, \] if we set widetildel_i:=l_i-fracw'rr_i and widetildel_I:=sum_iin Iwidetildel_i, then c_1(nu^* P_L)-c_1(nu^* delta_w') = sum_i=1^k nu_i widetildel_i = sum_i=1^k-1widetildel_I_i(nu_i-nu_i+1), where I_i=\1,ldots,i\. Also, by Lemma~, we have frac12c_1(nu^* L_H_b^>0) = (g-1)sum_i<jr_i r_j(nu_i-nu_j) = (g-1)sum_i=1^k-1 r_I_ir_I_i^circ(nu_i-nu_i+1), where I^circ denotes the complement of I. Suppose that L corresponds to a semistable Higgs bundle. For any subset Isubset \1,ldots,k\, we have the exact sequence \[ 0 to L|_C_I^circ(-C_I) to L to L|_C_I to 0 . \] The semistability of L gives (see Remark~) \[ fracdeg pi_*Lrank pi_*L leqslant fracdeg pi_*(L|_C_I) rank pi_*(L|_C_I), \] or equivalently (using ()) \[ fracw'-(r^2-r)(g-1)r leqslant fracl_I-(r_I^2-r_I)(g-1)r_I. \] Expanding this inequality, we obtain \[ widetildel_I := l_I-fracr_Irw' geqslant -(g-1)r_I r_I^circ. \] Replacing I with I^circ and using widetildel_I+widetildel_I^circ=0, we also obtain widetildel_I leqslant (g-1)r_I r_I^circ. Hence, by () and (), the condition~() holds. Conversely, suppose that L is not semistable. Then there is an exact sequence in Coh^heartsuit(C_b) \[ 0to E_2 to L to E_1 to 0 \] such that fracdeg pi_*Lrank pi_*L> fracdeg pi_*E_1rank pi_*E_1. By taking the saturation, we can take E_1 to be torsion-free on C_b. Then the induced surjection O_C_b twoheadrightarrow E_1 otimes L^-1 gives E_1 otimes L^-1cong O_C_1' for a decomposition C_b=C_1'+C_2' as effective divisors on S. Writing r_i'=rank(pi_*O_C_i') and l_i'=deg_C_i'(L|_C_i'), the inequality~() is equivalent to \[ fracw'-(r^2-r)(g-1)r > fracl_1'-(r_1^'2-r_1')(g-1)r_1'. \] Expanding this inequality gives \[ widetildel_1' := l_1'-fracr_1'rw' < -(g-1)r_1' r_2'. \] It follows that, for any map nu'colon BG_m to H_b of the form pt mapsto M_1'oplus M_2' with Supp(M_i')=C_i' and G_m-weights (nu_1', nu_2') with nu_1'>nu_2', we have c_1((nu')^* P_L) -c_1((nu')^* delta_w') &= widetildel_1'(nu_1'-nu_2') \\ &< -(g-1)r_1' r_2'(nu_1'-nu_2') \\ &= frac12c_1((nu')^*L_H_b^<0). Therefore the condition~() is not satisfied.
nodes.raw_latex:
Let $\nu \colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathcal{H}_b$ be a map as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:PLGm}, and set $r_i=\operatorname{rank}(\pi_{*}\mathcal{O}_{C_i})$, 
$l_i=\deg_{C_i}(\mathcal{L}|_{C_i})$.  For a subset
$I\subset \{1,\ldots,k\}$, we write
$C_I:=\sum_{i\in I} C_i$ as an effective divisor on $S$, and set
$r_I:=\sum_{i\in I}r_i$ and $l_I:=\sum_{i\in I}l_i$. 
Note that $\mathrm{wt}(\nu^* \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{L}})$ consists of the single element
$c_1(\nu^* \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{L}})\in \mathbb{Z}$, as $\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{L}}$ is a line bundle.
Since
\[
c_1(\nu^* \delta_{w'})
=
\frac{w'}{r}\sum_{i=1}^k r_i \nu_i,
\]
if we set
$\widetilde{l}_i:=l_i-\frac{w'}{r}r_i$ and
$\widetilde{l}_I:=\sum_{i\in I}\widetilde{l}_i$, then
\begin{align}\label{eq:c1P}
c_1(\nu^* \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{L}})-c_1(\nu^* \delta_{w'})
=
\sum_{i=1}^k \nu_i \widetilde{l}_i
=
\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}\widetilde{l}_{I_i}(\nu_i-\nu_{i+1}),
\end{align}
where $I_i=\{1,\ldots,i\}$. Also, by Lemma~\ref{lem:Gmwt:L}, we have
\begin{align}\label{eq:Lpos}
    \frac{1}{2}c_1(\nu^* \mathbb{L}_{\mathcal{H}_b}^{>0})
    =
    (g-1)\sum_{i<j}r_i r_j(\nu_i-\nu_j)
    =
    (g-1)\sum_{i=1}^{k-1}
    r_{I_i}r_{I_i^{\circ}}(\nu_i-\nu_{i+1}),
\end{align}
where $I^{\circ}$ denotes the complement of $I$.

Suppose that $\mathcal{L}$ corresponds to a semistable Higgs bundle.
For any subset $I\subset \{1,\ldots,k\}$, we have the exact sequence
\[
0 \to \mathcal{L}|_{C_{I^{\circ}}}(-C_I) \to \mathcal{L}
\to \mathcal{L}|_{C_I} \to 0 .
\]
The semistability of $\mathcal{L}$ gives (see Remark~\ref{rmk:ss:spec})
\[
\frac{\deg \pi_{*}\mathcal{L}}{\operatorname{rank} \pi_{*}\mathcal{L}}
\leqslant
\frac{\deg \pi_{*}(\mathcal{L}|_{C_I})}
     {\operatorname{rank} \pi_{*}(\mathcal{L}|_{C_I})},
\]
or equivalently (using (\ref{formula:deg}))
\[
\frac{w'-(r^2-r)(g-1)}{r}
\leqslant
\frac{l_I-(r_I^2-r_I)(g-1)}{r_I}.
\]
Expanding this inequality, we obtain
\[
    \widetilde{l}_I
    :=
    l_I-\frac{r_I}{r}w'
    \geqslant
    -(g-1)r_I r_{I^{\circ}}.
\]
Replacing $I$ with $I^{\circ}$ and using
$\widetilde{l}_I+\widetilde{l}_{I^{\circ}}=0$, we also obtain
$\widetilde{l}_I \leqslant (g-1)r_I r_{I^{\circ}}$. Hence, by
(\ref{eq:c1P}) and (\ref{eq:Lpos}), the condition~(\ref{nuPL}) holds.

Conversely, suppose that $\mathcal{L}$ is not semistable. Then there is
an exact sequence in $\operatorname{Coh}^{\heartsuit}(\mathcal{C}_b)$
\[
    0\to E_2 \to \mathcal{L} \to E_1 \to 0
\]
such that
\begin{align}\label{ineq:LE}
\frac{\deg \pi_{*}\mathcal{L}}{\operatorname{rank} \pi_{*}\mathcal{L}}>
\frac{\deg \pi_{*}E_1}{\operatorname{rank} \pi_{*}E_1}.
\end{align}
By taking the saturation, we can take $E_1$ to be torsion-free on $\mathcal{C}_b$. 
Then the induced surjection
$\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}_b} \twoheadrightarrow E_1 \otimes \mathcal{L}^{-1}$
gives $E_1 \otimes \mathcal{L}^{-1}\cong \mathcal{O}_{C_1'}$ for a decomposition
$\mathcal{C}_b=C_1'+C_2'$ as effective divisors on $S$. Writing
$r_i'=\operatorname{rank}(\pi_{*}\mathcal{O}_{C_i'})$ and
$l_i'=\deg_{C_i'}(\mathcal{L}|_{C_i'})$, the inequality~(\ref{ineq:LE}) is
equivalent to
\[
\frac{w'-(r^2-r)(g-1)}{r}
>
\frac{l_1'-(r_1^{'2}-r_1')(g-1)}{r_1'}.
\]
Expanding this inequality gives
\[
    \widetilde{l}_1'
    :=
    l_1'-\frac{r_1'}{r}w'
    <
    -(g-1)r_1' r_2'.
\]
It follows that, for any map $\nu'\colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathcal{H}_b$ of the form
$\mathrm{pt} \mapsto M_1'\oplus M_2'$ with
$\mathrm{Supp}(M_i')=C_i'$ and $\mathbb{G}_m$-weights $(\nu_1', \nu_2')$
with 
$\nu_1'>\nu_2'$, we have
\begin{align*}
   c_1((\nu')^* \mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{L}})
   -c_1((\nu')^* \delta_{w'})
   &=
   \widetilde{l}_1'(\nu_1'-\nu_2')  \\
   &<
   -(g-1)r_1' r_2'(\nu_1'-\nu_2') \\
   &=
   \frac{1}{2}c_1((\nu')^*\mathbb{L}_{\mathcal{H}_b}^{<0}).
\end{align*}
Therefore the condition~(\ref{nuPL}) is not satisfied.

The assertion is local at the singular points and follows from the classification of rank-one torsion-free modules over the complete local rings 
$k[[x,y]]/(y^2-x^m)$. Indeed from~\cite[Lemma~4.26]{TodaGL2}, there is a line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ on $\mathcal{C}_b$
and an injection $\mathcal{L} \hookrightarrow E$, which is an isomorphism at 
the locus where $E$ is a line bundle on $\mathcal{C}_b$, such that

nodes.raw_latex:
It is enough to show that each irreducible component of $\mathcal{H}ecke_{\mathcal{D}_p}$ which contains the image of $\tau_0$
    is dominant over $\mathcal{B}$
    under the map $\mathcal{H}ecke_{\mathcal{D}_p} \to \mathcal{B}$, following the first part of the proof of~\cite[Lemma~5.3]{TodaGL2}. Indeed suppose that the above statement holds. Let $W\to \mathcal{H}ecke_{\mathcal{D}_p}$ be an atlas with a point $p'\in W$ 
which maps to $\tau_0$, and take an irreducible component $p' \in W' \subset W$. 
We take a resolution of singularities $W'' \to W'$ and a lift $p'' \in W''$ of $p'$. Then we take a smooth affine open neighborhood 
$p''\in W'''$; by the construction $W''' \to \mathcal{B}$ is dominant. A desired $(\Delta, 0)$ is 
constructed by taking a generic hypersurface $0=p'' \in \Delta \subset W'''$
if $\ell<\dim W'''$, or if $\ell \geqslant \dim W'''$ take $\Delta=W''' \times \mathbb{A}^{\ell-\dim W'''}$, $0=(p'', 0)$ and construct a map $\Delta \to \mathcal{H}ecke_{\mathcal{D}_p}$ by 
composing with the projection $\Delta \to W'''$.

We have the factorization 
\begin{align}\label{factor:Hecke}
    \mathcal{H}ecke_{\mathcal{D}_p} \to \mathcal{H}ecke \stackrel{\mathrm{ev}_2}{\to} \mathcal{H} \stackrel{h}{\to} \mathcal{B}.
\end{align}
The first map $\mathcal{H}ecke_{\mathcal{D}_p} \to \mathcal{H}ecke$ is \'{e}tale, as it is obtained by 
an \'{e}tale base change from the diagram~\eqref{dia:heckeD}.
The second map $\mathrm{ev}_2$ is flat and surjective by Lemma~\ref{lem:heckeclass}.
The last map $h$ is also flat and surjective by Theorem~\ref{thm:higgs:basic}. 
It follows that the composition~\eqref{factor:Hecke} is flat. 
Since $\mathcal{B}$ is irreducible, every irreducible component of 
$\mathcal{H}ecke_{\mathcal{D}_p}$ dominates $\mathcal{B}$ under a flat morphism. 
Therefore, for each irreducible component 
$\mathcal{Z} \subset \mathcal{H}ecke_{\mathcal{D}_p}$, the morphism 
$\mathcal{Z} \to \mathcal{B}$ is dominant.

The proof is the same as~\cite[Proposition~5.11]{TodaGL2}, but we include it for completeness.
Let $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{sg}} \subset \mathcal{B}$ be the closed subset corresponding 
to the singular spectral curves. It is of codimension one, and its 
generic point corresponds to those with at worst nodal singularities, see Lemma~\ref{lem:nodeB} below. 
Then we can take $\Delta$ so that $\dim \Delta =2$ and 
the image of the composition 
\begin{align*}\Delta \setminus \{0\} \hookrightarrow \Delta \to \mathcal{B}
\end{align*}
corresponds to the locus of spectral curves which are either smooth or have at worst nodal singularities. Then, from Lemma~\ref{lem:nodal}, the sequence (\ref{extend:CM}) is 
exact on $\Delta \setminus \{0\}$. 

Assume that the sequence (\ref{extend:CM}) is not exact.
Let $\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}$ be the complex (\ref{extend:CM})
regarded as an object in $\operatorname{Coh}(\mathcal{H}_{\Delta})$, where 
$\mathcal{P}_{\Delta 2}$ is located in degree zero. 
Since (\ref{extend:CM}) is left exact, the object $\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}$ is a non-zero object
in $\operatorname{Coh}^{\heartsuit}(\mathcal{H}_{\Delta})$ and supported 
over $0\in \Delta$. 
Let $i \colon \Delta' \subset \Delta$ be a generic smooth divisor 
such that $0\in \Delta'$.
We use the same notation $i$ for the induced map $i \colon \mathcal{H}_{\Delta'} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{H}_{\Delta}$. 
Then as $\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}$ is supported over $0\in \Delta'$, 
it follows that 
\begin{align*}
0\neq \mathcal{H}^{-1}(i^* \mathbb{P}_{\Delta}) \in \operatorname{Coh}^{\heartsuit}(\mathcal{H}_{\Delta'}).
\end{align*}

On the other hand, 
since each term of $\mathbb{P}_{\Delta}$ is flat over $\Delta$, 
we have $i^* \mathbb{P}_{\Delta}=\mathbb{P}_{\Delta'}$ and it 
lies in $\operatorname{Coh}^{\heartsuit}(\mathcal{H}_{\Delta'})$ by
the left exactness of
the sequence 
   \begin{align}\notag
        0\to \mathcal{P}_{\Delta' 2}^{\sigma}\to \mathcal{V}_{\Delta'}\otimes \mathcal{P}_{\Delta' 1}
        \to \mathcal{P}_{\Delta' 2}
    \end{align}
    which is obtained as in 
(\ref{extend:CM}) by replacing $\Delta$ with $\Delta'$. 
It contradicts $\mathcal{H}^{-1}(i^*\mathbb{P}_{\Delta})\neq 0$,
hence the sequence (\ref{extend:CM}) is exact. 
Then by taking the restriction of (\ref{extend:CM}) to $0\in \Delta$, 
we conclude that the sequence (\ref{extend:CM2}) is exact.

The case $g\geqslant 3$ follows from~\cite[Corollary~1.5 and Remark~1.7]{KouvidakisPantev1995}. 
Indeed, it is proven in loc. cit. that the locus 
$\mathrm{B}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}^{\mathrm{sg}} \subset \mathrm{B}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ corresponding to singular 
spectral curves is an irreducible hypersurface, and that there exists 
$b\in \mathrm{B}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}^{\mathrm{sg}}$ such that $\mathcal{C}_b$ is irreducible with only one node. 
Therefore the generic point of $\mathrm{B}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}^{\mathrm{sg}}$ corresponds to an 
irreducible curve with only one nodal singularity. 
It follows that the complement of $\mathrm{B}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}^{\mathrm{node}}$ in 
$\mathrm{B}_{\operatorname{GL}_r}^{\mathrm{cl}}$ has codimension at least two.

The case $g=2$ has to be treated separately, which we prove in Subsection~\ref{subsec:g=2}.

Let $Q=\bigoplus_{p\in N}Q_p$ be the zero-dimensional sheaf as in the exact sequence (\ref{exact:LE}). 
We prove the proposition by induction on $\chi(Q)\geqslant 0$. 
The base case, $\chi(Q)=0$, is obvious since $E=\mathcal{L}$ 
and $\mathcal{P}_E=\mathcal{V}_{E}$ in this case. 

Suppose that $\chi(Q)>0$. 
    By Proposition~\ref{prop:exact2}, 
    there is an exact sequence of the form 
    \begin{align*}
        \cdots\to \mathcal{V}_{p}\otimes \mathcal{P}_{E'} \to \mathcal{V}_p\otimes \mathcal{P}_{E'} \to 
        \mathcal{V}_p\otimes \mathcal{P}_{E'} \to \mathcal{P}_E \to 0.
    \end{align*}
    Since $\chi(Q')=\chi(Q)-1$ in the sequence (\ref{exact:E2}), 
    we can apply the induction hypothesis for $\mathcal{P}_{E'}$. Then the claim 
    for $\mathcal{P}_E$ holds by the above exact sequence together with 
    $\mathcal{V}_p\otimes \mathcal{V}_{E'}\cong \mathcal{V}_E$.

Its complement Z is a closed substack which is disjoint from the closed substack overlines_T(T). Put $Z:=C_1\cap C_2$.  Since $E_i$ is a line bundle along $Z$, it is
enough to construct an extension which is locally, at every point of
$Z$, the standard extension
\[
0\to I_{C_2/\mathcal{C}}\to \mathcal O_{\mathcal{C}}\to \mathcal O_{C_2}\to 0 .
\]
Indeed, as $\mathcal{C}$ is reduced and planar, 
we have an isomorphism $I_{C_2/C, p} \cong \mathcal{O}_{C_1, p}$. 
Thus the above standard sequence at $p$ is an extension of
$\mathcal O_{C_2,p}$ by $\mathcal O_{C_1,p}$ whose middle term is
$\mathcal O_{\mathcal{C},p}$.

Using local trivializations of $E_i$ along $Z$, these standard local
extensions give a section of
$
\mathcal Ext^1_{\mathcal{C}}(E_2,E_1)$, 
which is supported on the finite scheme $Z$.  Since $\mathcal{C}$ is a curve,
the local-to-global Ext sequence gives a surjection
\[
\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal{C}}(E_2,E_1)
\twoheadrightarrow
H^0\bigl(\mathcal{C},\mathcal Ext^1_{\mathcal{C}}(E_2,E_1)\bigr).
\]
Hence the above local extension classes lift to a global extension
\[
0\to E_1\to E\to E_2\to 0 .
\]
By construction, after localizing at any $p\in Z$, this extension is
isomorphic to the standard one.  Therefore
$E_p\cong \mathcal O_{\mathcal{C},p}$ for all $p\in Z$, so $E$ is a line bundle
along $C_1\cap C_2$.

Since both sides are maximal Cohen--Macaulay sheaves, it is enough 
   to show the isomorphism over the open substack 
   \begin{align*}((\mathcal{H}_{\circ}(w_0)^{\mathrm{reg}}\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\circ}}\mathcal{H}_{\circ})
   \cup (\mathcal{H}_{\circ}(w_0)\times_{\mathcal{B}_{\circ}}\mathcal{H}_{\circ}^{\mathrm{reg}}))\times \operatorname{Pic}(C)
   \end{align*}
   since its complement has codimension at least two. 
We take a $k$-valued point $(A, B, M)$ of the above substack, namely $A, B \in \operatorname{Coh}^{\heartsuit}(\mathcal{C}_b)$ such that either one of them is a line bundle, $M$ is a line bundle on $C$.
   By the multiplicative property of Deligne pairing~\cite[Section~6.2]{Deligne1987Determinant}, we have 
   \begin{align*}
       \alpha^* \mathcal{P}_{\circ}|_{(A, B, M)} \cong 
       \mathcal{P}_{\circ}|_{(A, B\otimes \pi^* M)} 
       \cong \mathcal{P}_{\circ}|_{(A, B)}\otimes \mathcal{P}_{\circ}|_{(A, \pi^*M)}.
   \end{align*}
   We have the isomorphisms
   \begin{align*}
    &\mathcal{P}_{\circ}|_{(A, \pi^*M)} \\
    &\cong   
    \det \chi(\pi_{*}A\otimes M)\otimes \det \chi(\pi_{*}A)^{-1}\otimes \det \chi(M\otimes \pi_{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}_b})^{-1}\otimes 
    \det \chi(\pi_{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}_b}) \\
    &\cong \mathcal{P}_C|_{(\det \pi_{*}A, M)}\otimes \mathcal{P}_{C}|_{(\det \pi_{*}\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}_b}, M)}^{-1} \\
    &\cong \mathcal{P}_{C}|_{(\mathrm{Nm}(A), M)}.
   \end{align*}

\label{lem:eta}
For $\nu \colon B\mathbb{G}_m \to \mathfrak{M}_{\circ}$ with image $x\in \mathfrak{M}_{\circ}(k)$, let $\nu_{\circ}^{\mathrm{reg}}$, 
$\nu^{\mathrm{reg}}$ be the regularization maps for $\mathfrak{M}_{\circ}$, 
$\mathfrak{M}$, respectively as in Subsection~\ref{subsec:variant}. Then 
for $\mathcal{E} \in \operatorname{Coh}(\mathfrak{M}_{\circ})$, we have 
\begin{align*}
    \mathrm{wt}(\iota_{*}\nu_{\circ}^{\mathrm{reg}*} \mathcal{E})=\mathrm{wt}(\iota_{*}\nu^{\mathrm{reg}*}i_{*}\mathcal{E})
    =\mathrm{wt}(\iota_{*}\nu^{\mathrm{reg}*}\eta^* \mathcal{E}).
\end{align*}
In particular for $\delta \in \mathrm{Pic}(\mathfrak{M})_{\mathbb{R}}$
with its restriction $\delta\in \mathrm{Pic}(\mathfrak{M}_{\circ})_{\mathbb{R}}$, 
we have $\mathcal{E} \in \widetilde{\operatorname{L}}(\mathfrak{M}_{\circ})_{\delta}$ if and only 
if $i_{*}\mathcal{E} \in \widetilde{\operatorname{L}}(\mathfrak{M})_{\delta}$, if and only if 
$\eta^*\mathcal{E} \in \widetilde{\operatorname{L}}(\mathfrak{M})_{\delta}$.

By applying the H^0(Omega_C)-action , and using the fact that Omega_C is globally generated, and that this action does not change the singularity type of C_b, we may assume that lambda=0. Thus we obtain a map \[ j_z colon B_GL_r^cl to J_z, \ bmapsto widehatF_b. \] We show that this map is surjective when rgeqslant 4. Noting that z=(c, 0), the map j_z is described as j_z colon B_GL_r^cl to koplus kxoplus kyoplus kx^2oplus kxyoplus ky^2 and is given by \[ (b_i)_1leqslant ileqslant r mapsto bigl( widehatb_r(0), widehatb_r-1(0), widehatb_r'(0), widehatb_r-2(0), widehatb_r-1'(0), widehatb_r''(0) bigr). \] Here widehatb_i denotes the image of b_i under the map \[ H^0(C,Omega_C^i)to widehatOmega_C,c^icong k[[x]]. \] It is enough to show that H^0(C,Omega_C^r-j) to Omega_C^r-jotimes O_C/m_c^3-j is surjective for 0leqslant jleqslant 2.
